title: Regional incident command
subtitle: Three regions → signature counts → incident brief
source:
define a program named frequency_row
  accept path as text
  accept pattern as text
  accept report as text
  read path
  then "grep" with arguments ["-F", "--", pattern] and keep status as matched
  then count lines
  then parse json as observed
  take integer at "" from observed as count
  run "printf" with arguments ["%d | %s\n", count, pattern]
  then save to report

# Merge real regional evidence, group signatures, and publish an incident brief.
define a program named count_matches
  accept path as text
  accept pattern as text
  accept report as text
  read path
  then "grep" with arguments ["-F", "--", pattern] and keep status as matched
  then save to report
  then count lines
  then parse json as measured
  take integer at "" from measured as count
  then encode count as json

run "cat" with arguments ["incident-us-east.log", "incident-eu-west.log", "incident-ap-south.log"]
then save to "incident-all.log"
read "incident-all.log"
then count lines
then parse json as events_json
take integer at "" from events_json as events
run program count_matches with path "incident-all.log" and pattern "ERROR" and report "incident-error-events.log"
then parse json as errors_json
take integer at "" from errors_json as errors
run program count_matches with path "incident-all.log" and pattern "WARN" and report "incident-warning-events.log"
then parse json as warnings_json
take integer at "" from warnings_json as warnings
read "incident-error-events.log"
then sort
pipe to "uniq" as error_signatures
then save to "incident-errors.txt"
read "incident-warning-events.log"
then sort
pipe to "uniq" as warning_signatures
then save to "incident-warnings.txt"
if errors is 0
  run "printf" with arguments ["CLEAR"] as state
otherwise
  run "printf" with arguments ["REVIEW REQUIRED"] as state
run "printf" with arguments ["{\"title\":\"Regional incident command\",\"status\":\"%s\",\"metrics\":[{\"label\":\"Events scanned\",\"value\":%d},{\"label\":\"Error events\",\"value\":%d},{\"label\":\"Warning events\",\"value\":%d}],\"notes\":[\"Counts come from three regional logs.\",\"Repeated signatures are grouped in incident-errors.txt.\"]}\n", state, events, errors, warnings]
then save to "incident-dashboard.json"
read "incident-regions.json"
then parse json as region_catalog
take list of text at "" from region_catalog as regions
for each region in regions
  run "printf" with arguments ["incident-region-%s.txt", region] as report_path
  run program frequency_row with path "incident-all.log" and pattern region and report report_path
run "cat" with arguments ["incident-region-us-east.txt", "incident-region-eu-west.txt", "incident-region-ap-south.txt"] as regional_frequencies
then save to "incident-regions.txt"
run "printf" with arguments ["╔══════════════════════════════════════════════════════════╗\n║  REGIONAL INCIDENT COMMAND                               ║\n╚══════════════════════════════════════════════════════════╝\n\nSTATE       %s\nCOVERAGE    us-east · eu-west · ap-south\nSCANNED     %d events\nERRORS      %d events\nWARNINGS    %d events\n\nREGIONAL EVENT FREQUENCIES · count | region\n%s\nUNIQUE ERROR SIGNATURES\n%s\nUNIQUE WARNING SIGNATURES\n%s\nARTIFACTS\n  incident-all.log       merged evidence, original order\n  incident-errors.txt    distinct error signatures\n  incident-regions.txt   exact regional event counts\n  incident-warnings.txt  distinct warning signatures\n  incident-dashboard.json  derived dashboard\n\nNEXT MOVE   Edit a regional log, run again, inspect the delta.\n", state, events, errors, warnings, regional_frequencies, error_signatures, warning_signatures]

title: Release launch control
subtitle: Typed gates → regional plans → a launch decision
source:
# A failing release stays held; all regional plans are still reviewable.
define a program named regional_checklist
  accept plan as text
  accept version as text
  accept decision as text
  accept passed as integer
  accept failed as integer
  accept canary as integer
  run "printf" with arguments ["REGIONAL ROLLOUT CHECKLIST\nArtifact: %s\nCandidate: %s\nDecision: %s\nTests passed: %d\nTests failed: %d\nCanary allocation: %d percent\n\n1. Confirm regional owner and rollback contact.\n2. Verify the test gate before changing traffic.\n3. Start with the declared canary allocation.\n4. Observe errors and latency before promotion.\n5. Record the final decision in the release review.\n", plan, version, decision, passed, failed, canary]
  then save to plan

read "launch-candidate.json"
then parse json as candidate
take text at "/version" from candidate as version
take boolean at "/checks_passed" from candidate as ready
take integer at "/tests_passed" from candidate as passed
take integer at "/tests_failed" from candidate as failed
take integer at "/canary_percent" from candidate as canary
take list of text at "/plan_files" from candidate as plans
if ready is true
  if failed is 0
    run "printf" with arguments ["READY FOR CANARY"] as decision
    run "printf" with arguments ["Checks passed. Request the regional owner review before a canary."] as guidance
  otherwise
    run "printf" with arguments ["HOLD"] as decision
    run "printf" with arguments ["The gate claims success but failed tests remain. Resolve the inconsistency."] as guidance
otherwise
  run "printf" with arguments ["HOLD"] as decision
  run "printf" with arguments ["Release is blocked until the JSON check gate passes."] as guidance
for each plan in plans
  run program regional_checklist with plan plan and version version and decision decision and passed passed and failed failed and canary canary
then encode plans as json
then save to "rollout-index.json"
read "rollout-index.json" as plan_index
run "printf" with arguments ["{\"title\":\"Release launch control\",\"status\":\"%s\",\"metrics\":[{\"label\":\"Tests passed\",\"value\":%d},{\"label\":\"Tests failed\",\"value\":%d},{\"label\":\"Canary traffic percent\",\"value\":%d}],\"notes\":[\"%s\",\"Regional checklists are generated even while the gate is held.\"]}\n", decision, passed, failed, canary, guidance]
then save to "launch-dashboard.json"
run "printf" with arguments ["╔══════════════════════════════════════════════════════════╗\n║  RELEASE LAUNCH CONTROL                                  ║\n╚══════════════════════════════════════════════════════════╝\n\nCANDIDATE   %s\nDECISION    %s\nTESTS       %d passed / %d failed\nCANARY      %d percent\n\nOPERATOR GUIDANCE\n%s\n\nREGIONAL ARTIFACT INDEX\n%s\n\nHANDOFF PACKAGE\n  rollout-*.txt         one checklist per declared region\n  rollout-index.json    exact generated artifact list\n  launch-dashboard.json  typed release metrics\n  launch-brief.txt      this reviewable launch brief\n\nTRY IT      Fix tests_failed and checks_passed in launch-candidate.json.\n", version, decision, passed, failed, canary, guidance, plan_index]
then save to "launch-brief.txt"

title: Web traffic: top endpoints
subtitle: nginx log → busiest requests, status codes, 5xx
source:
# Rank requests and count status codes in a compact nginx access log.
# Log format: log_format compact '$request_method $uri $status';
accept top as integer with default 5
accept codes as list of text with default ["200", "201", "301", "304", "401", "404", "500", "502", "504"]

define a program named tally
  accept path as text
  accept pattern as text
  read path

  then count lines
  then parse json as measured
  take integer at "" from measured as count
  then encode count as json

read "nginx-access.log"
then count lines
then parse json as total_json
take integer at "" from total_json as total

# Busiest requests: sort, count adjacent duplicates, rank by count.
read "nginx-access.log"
then sort
pipe to "uniq" with arguments ["-c"]
pipe to "sort" with arguments ["-r"]
pipe to "head" with arguments ["-n", top] as busiest

# One row per status code that actually appears.
run "printf" with arguments [""] as table
for each code in codes

# Triage failed SSH logins in an auth log: which accounts and networks are hit,

accept networks as list of text with default ["203.0.113.", "192.0.2.", "198.51.100."]

# Count lines of one file that contain both literal patterns.

  then "grep" with arguments ["-F", "--", pattern] and keep status as matched
  then count lines
  then parse json as measured
  take integer at "" from measured as count
  then encode count as json

run program tally with path "auth.log" and scope "sshd" and pattern "Failed password" as failed
run program tally with path "auth.log" and scope "sshd" and pattern "Invalid user" as invalid
run program tally with path "auth.log" and scope "sshd" and pattern "Accepted" as accepted

title: Listening ports audit
subtitle: ss output → unexpected public listeners
source:
# Audit listening TCP sockets from ss -tlnp against an allowlist.
#   ss -tlnp > ss-listen.txt
# Loopback listeners are ignored. Anything else must be on the allowlist, and some ports must never be public.
define a program named count_of
  accept text as text
  use value text
  then count lines
  then parse json as measured
  take integer at "" from measured as count
  then encode count as json

read "allowed-ports.json"
then parse json as policy
take list of text at "/public" from policy as allowed
take list of text at "/never_public" from policy as never_public

# Public listeners: remove the header and every loopback address.
read "ss-listen.txt"
then "grep" with arguments ["-F", "-v", "--", "State"] and keep status as s1
then "grep" with arguments ["-F", "-v", "--", "127."] and keep status as s2
then "grep" with arguments ["-F", "-v", "--", "[::1]"] as public and keep status as s3
run program count_of with text public as public_count

# Unexpected listeners: the list flows through the loop, and each allowed port is filtered out of it.
use value public
for each port in allowed
  then "grep" with arguments ["-F", "-v", "--", port] and keep status as kept
then "cat" as unexpected
run program count_of with text unexpected as unexpected_count

run "printf" with arguments [""] as exposed
for each port in never_public
  if public contains port
    run "printf" with arguments ["%sCRITICAL  %sis reachable from outside\n", exposed, port] as exposed

if unexpected_count is "0"
  run "printf" with arguments ["CLEAN"] as verdict
otherwise
  run "printf" with arguments ["REVIEW: %s unexpected public listeners", unexpected_count] as verdict

run "printf" with arguments ["%s\n%s public listeners, %s unexpected.\n\nNot on the allowlist\n%s\nPorts that must never be public\n%s", verdict, public_count, unexpected_count, unexpected, exposed]
expected:
REVIEW: 3 unexpected public listeners
9 public listeners, 3 unexpected.

Not on the allowlist
LISTEN 0      511          0.0.0.0:6379       0.0.0.0:*     users:(("redis-server",pid=1011,fd=6))
LISTEN 0      4096         0.0.0.0:9100       0.0.0.0:*     users:(("node_exporter",pid=3315,fd=3))
LISTEN 0      128          0.0.0.0:8080       0.0.0.0:*     users:(("java",pid=2210,fd=44))

source:
# Audit /etc/passwd and /etc/group copies for accounts that deserve a second look.
accept admins as text with default "ada,deploy"
accept shells as list of text with default ["/bin/bash", "/bin/zsh", "/bin/sh", "/bin/fish"]

source:
# Disk and inode report from two df snapshots.
#   df -h --output=pcent,size,used,avail,target > df.txt
#   df -i --output=ipcent,itotal,iused,iavail,target > df-inodes.txt

  then count lines
  then parse json as measured
  take integer at "" from measured as count
  then encode count as json

  accept path as text
  accept levels as list of text
  run "printf" with arguments [""] as rows
  for each level in levels
    read path
    then "grep" with arguments ["-F", "--", level] as hits and keep status as matched
    run "printf" with arguments ["%s%s", rows, hits] as rows
  run "printf" with arguments ["%s", rows]
  then "sort" with arguments ["-r"]

run program lines_in with path "df.txt" as filesystems
run program critical_rows with path "df.txt" and levels critical as full_space

then count lines
then parse json as space_json

title: Service health dashboard
subtitle: Health JSON → up, degraded, down
source:
# Turn a health-check API response into a service dashboard and a list of what to look at first.
# The status and every number come from the response, not from this script's own assumptions.
define a program named count_of
  accept text as text
  use value text
  then count lines
  then parse json as measured
  take integer at "" from measured as count
  then encode count as json

read "health.json"
then parse json as response
take text at "/checked_at" from response as checked_at
take json at "/services" from response as services

run "printf" with arguments [""] as up
run "printf" with arguments [""] as degraded
run "printf" with arguments [""] as down
run "printf" with arguments [""] as notes
run "printf" with arguments [""] as separator
for each service in services
  take text at "/name" from service as name
  take text at "/state" from service as state
  take integer at "/latency_ms" from service as latency
  take text at "/detail" from service as detail
  if state is "up"
    run "printf" with arguments ["%s%s\n", up, name] as up
  otherwise if state is "degraded"
    run "printf" with arguments ["%s%s  %d ms  %s\n", degraded, name, latency, detail] as degraded
    run "printf" with arguments ["%s%s\"%s degraded: %s\"", notes, separator, name, detail] as notes
    run "printf" with arguments [","] as separator
  otherwise
    run "printf" with arguments ["%s%s  %s\n", down, name, detail] as down
    run "printf" with arguments ["%s%s\"%s DOWN: %s\"", notes, separator, name, detail] as notes
    run "printf" with arguments [","] as separator

run program count_of with text up as up_count
run program count_of with text degraded as degraded_count
run program count_of with text down as down_count
run "printf" with arguments ["%s%s%s", up, degraded, down]
then count lines
then parse json as total_json
take integer at "" from total_json as total

if down_count is "0"
  if degraded_count is "0"
    run "printf" with arguments ["ALL SERVICES UP"] as status
  otherwise
    run "printf" with arguments ["DEGRADED"] as status
otherwise
  run "printf" with arguments ["OUTAGE"] as status

then save to "health-dashboard.json"

run "printf" with arguments ["%s at %s\n\nDown (fix first)\n%s\nDegraded\n%s\nUp\n%s", status, checked_at, down, degraded, up]

title: Certificate expiry check
subtitle: Cert inventory → expired, expiring, OK
source:
# Check certificate expiry dates from an inventory export.
# Dates are ISO (YYYY-MM-DD), so sorting two of them as text puts the earlier one first.
accept today as text with default "2026-10-17"
accept warn_by as text described as "Warn about certificates that expire before this date" with default "2026-11-16"

define a program named before
  accept a as text
  accept b as text
  run "printf" with arguments ["%s\n%s\n", a, b]
  then "sort"
  then "head" with arguments ["-n", "1"] as first
  run "printf" with arguments ["%s\n", a] as a_line
  if a is b
    run "printf" with arguments ["no"]
  otherwise if first is a_line
    run "printf" with arguments ["yes"]
  otherwise
    run "printf" with arguments ["no"]

read "certs.json"
then parse json as inventory
take json at "/certs" from inventory as certs

run "printf" with arguments [""] as rows
for each cert in certs
  take text at "/host" from cert as host
  take text at "/not_after" from cert as expires
  take text at "/issuer" from cert as issuer
  run program before with a expires and b today as expired
  run program before with a expires and b warn_by as soon
  if expired is "yes"
    run "printf" with arguments ["%sEXPIRED   %s  %s  %s\n", rows, expires, host, issuer] as rows
  otherwise if soon is "yes"
    run "printf" with arguments ["%sEXPIRING  %s  %s  %s\n", rows, expires, host, issuer] as rows
  otherwise
    run "printf" with arguments ["%sOK        %s  %s  %s\n", rows, expires, host, issuer] as rows

# Status words sort as EXPIRED, EXPIRING, OK; the date after each word puts the soonest first.
use value rows
then "sort" as report
then count lines
then parse json as total_json
take integer at "" from total_json as total

use value report
then "grep" with arguments ["-F", "--", "EXPIRED "] and keep status as s1
then count lines
then parse json as expired_json
take integer at "" from expired_json as expired_count

use value report
then "grep" with arguments ["-F", "--", "EXPIRING "] and keep status as s2
then count lines
then parse json as expiring_json
take integer at "" from expiring_json as expiring_count

if expired_count is 0
  if expiring_count is 0
    run "printf" with arguments ["ALL CURRENT"] as status
  otherwise
    run "printf" with arguments ["RENEW SOON"] as status
otherwise
  run "printf" with arguments ["EXPIRED CERTIFICATES"] as status

run "printf" with arguments ["{\"title\":\"Certificate expiry\",\"status\":\"%s\",\"metrics\":[{\"label\":\"Certificates\",\"value\":%d},{\"label\":\"Expired\",\"value\":%d},{\"label\":\"Expiring before %s\",\"value\":%d}],\"notes\":[\"Dates compare as ISO text, so no date arithmetic is needed.\",\"Change today or warn_by in Inputs and run again.\"]}\n", status, total, expired_count, warn_by, expiring_count]
then save to "cert-dashboard.json"
run "printf" with arguments ["%s\ntoday %s, warning window ends %s\n\n%s", status, today, warn_by, report]
expected:
EXPIRED CERTIFICATES
today 2026-10-17, warning window ends 2026-11-16

EXPIRED   2026-10-14  www.example.com  R11
EXPIRED   2026-10-16  wiki.corp.example.com  Corp Issuing CA
EXPIRING  2026-10-17  vpn.example.com  Corp Issuing CA
EXPIRING  2026-10-20  api.example.com  R11
EXPIRING  2026-11-03  shop.example.com  R10
OK        2026-11-16  docs.example.com  R10
OK        2026-12-28  mail.example.com  R11
OK        2027-03-02  status.example.com  R11

title: Cron and timer audit
subtitle: cron.d + timers → risky or idle jobs
source:
# Audit a cron.d file and a systemctl timer listing for jobs worth a second look.
#   systemctl list-timers --all --no-pager > timers.txt

# Active jobs: drop comments and environment lines, keep lines that run a command.
define a program named active_jobs
  accept path as text
  read path
  then "grep" with arguments ["-F", "-v", "--", "#"] and keep status as s1
  then "grep" with arguments ["-F", "-v", "--", "MAILTO="] and keep status as s2
  then "grep" with arguments ["-F", "-v", "--", "SHELL="] and keep status as s3
  then "grep" with arguments ["-F", "-v", "--", "PATH="] and keep status as s4
  then "grep" with arguments ["-F", "--", "/"] and keep status as s5

define a program named count_of
  accept text as text
  use value text
  then count lines
  then parse json as measured
  take integer at "" from measured as count
  then encode count as json

run program active_jobs with path "crontab.txt" as jobs
run program count_of with text jobs as job_count

use value jobs
then "grep" with arguments ["-F", "--", " root "] as root_jobs and keep status as s6
run program count_of with text root_jobs as root_count

# Findings, one pattern each. Every finding names the line so it can be fixed.
run "printf" with arguments [""] as findings
for each rule in ["| sh", "| bash"]
  use value jobs
  then "grep" with arguments ["-F", "--", rule] as hits and keep status as s7
  run "printf" with arguments ["%s%s", findings, hits] as findings
run "printf" with arguments ["%s", findings] as pipes_to_shell

run "printf" with arguments [""] as quiet
for each rule in ["> /dev/null", ">/dev/null"]
  use value jobs
  then "grep" with arguments ["-F", "--", rule] as hits and keep status as s8
  run "printf" with arguments ["%s%s", quiet, hits] as quiet

use value jobs
then "grep" with arguments ["-F", "--", "@reboot"] as reboot_jobs and keep status as s9

# Timers whose next or last run is n/a are unscheduled or have never fired.
read "timers.txt"
then "grep" with arguments ["-F", "--", "n/a"] as idle_timers and keep status as s10
run program count_of with text idle_timers as idle_count

read "timers.txt"
then "grep" with arguments ["-F", "--", ".timer"] and keep status as s11
then count lines
then parse json as timers_json
take integer at "" from timers_json as timer_count

run "printf" with arguments ["%s active cron jobs, %s of them run as root. %s timers listed.\n\nHIGH  downloads a script and pipes it to a shell\n%s\nMEDIUM  output is thrown away, failures are invisible\n%s\nINFO  runs only at boot\n%s\nREVIEW  timers that are not scheduled or never ran (%s)\n%s", job_count, root_count, timer_count, pipes_to_shell, quiet, reboot_jobs, idle_count, idle_timers]
expected:
9 active cron jobs, 6 of them run as root. 6 timers listed.

HIGH  downloads a script and pipes it to a shell
0     4  *   *   0   root      curl -fsSL https://get.example.net/maintenance.sh | sh

MEDIUM  output is thrown away, failures are invisible
45    3  *   *   *   www-data  /usr/bin/php /var/www/cleanup.php > /dev/null 2>&1

INFO  runs only at boot
@reboot                root      /usr/local/bin/mount-scratch.sh

REVIEW  timers that are not scheduled or never ran (2)
n/a                         n/a           Mon 2026-08-03 10:00:01 UTC 2 months ago old-sync.timer              old-sync.service
n/a                         n/a           n/a                         n/a          legacy-report.timer          legacy-report.service
hint: Delete the curl line from crontab.txt and the HIGH finding disappears.

title: Env file validation
subtitle: .env + policy → missing, empty, sample values
source:
# Validate an .env file against a list of required keys. Required keys are reported by name only.
# Commented-out lines do not count as settings.
define a program named setting
  accept path as text
  accept key as text
  run "printf" with arguments ["%s=", key] as needle
  read path
  then "grep" with arguments ["-F", "-v", "--", "#"] and keep status as s1
  then "grep" with arguments ["-F", "--", needle] and keep status as s2
  then "head" with arguments ["-n", "1"]

read "required-env.json"
then parse json as policy
take list of text at "/required" from policy as required
take list of text at "/placeholders" from policy as placeholders
take list of text at "/discouraged" from policy as discouraged

run "printf" with arguments [""] as table
run "printf" with arguments [""] as problems
for each key in required
  run program setting with path "app.env" and key key as line
  run "printf" with arguments ["%s=\n", key] as empty_line
  if line is ""
    run "printf" with arguments ["%sMISSING      %s\n", table, key] as table
    run "printf" with arguments ["%s%s\n", problems, key] as problems
  otherwise if line is empty_line
    run "printf" with arguments ["%sEMPTY        %s\n", table, key] as table
    run "printf" with arguments ["%s%s\n", problems, key] as problems
  otherwise
    run "printf" with arguments ["ok"] as state
    for each word in placeholders
      if line contains word
        run "printf" with arguments ["placeholder"] as state
    if state is "ok"
      run "printf" with arguments ["%sok           %s\n", table, key] as table
    otherwise
      run "printf" with arguments ["%sPLACEHOLDER  %s (contains a sample value)\n", table, key] as table
      run "printf" with arguments ["%s%s\n", problems, key] as problems

run "printf" with arguments [""] as warnings
for each pattern in discouraged
  read "app.env"
  then "grep" with arguments ["-F", "-v", "--", "#"] and keep status as s3
  then "grep" with arguments ["-F", "--", pattern] as found and keep status as s4
  run "printf" with arguments ["%s%s", warnings, found] as warnings

use value problems
then count lines
then parse json as problem_json
take integer at "" from problem_json as problem_count

if problem_count is 0
  run "printf" with arguments ["VALID"] as verdict
otherwise
  run "printf" with arguments ["INVALID: %d keys need attention", problem_count] as verdict

run "printf" with arguments ["%s\n\n%s\nDiscouraged settings in production\n%s", verdict, table, warnings]
expected:
INVALID: 4 keys need attention

ok           PORT
ok           DATABASE_URL
ok           REDIS_URL
PLACEHOLDER  SECRET_KEY (contains a sample value)
EMPTY        SMTP_HOST
MISSING      SENTRY_DSN
MISSING      STRIPE_API_KEY

Discouraged settings in production
LOG_LEVEL=debug

title: sshd_config change review
subtitle: Old vs new file → diff and policy check
source:
# Review a proposed sshd_config against the running one and a hardening policy.
# Directive lines are unique, so each file is a set. Lines present in only one file are the change.

# Directives only: drop comments, keep lines of the form "Key value", sorted and unique.
define a program named directives
  accept path as text
  read path
  then "grep" with arguments ["-F", "-v", "--", "#"] and keep status as s1
  then "grep" with arguments ["-F", "--", " "] and keep status as s2
  then "sort" with arguments ["-u"]

run program directives with path "sshd_config.current" as current
run program directives with path "sshd_config.proposed" as proposed

# current once + proposed twice: a count of 1 means only in current, 2 means only in proposed, 3 means unchanged.
run "printf" with arguments ["%s%s%s", current, proposed, proposed]
then "sort"
pipe to "uniq" with arguments ["-c"] as tally

use value tally
then "grep" with arguments ["-F", "--", "      1 "] as removed and keep status as s3
use value tally
then "grep" with arguments ["-F", "--", "      2 "] as added and keep status as s4

use value removed
then count lines
then parse json as removed_json
take integer at "" from removed_json as removed_count
use value added
then count lines
then parse json as added_json
take integer at "" from added_json as added_count

read "sshd-policy.json"
then parse json as policy
take list of text at "/required" from policy as required
take list of text at "/forbidden" from policy as forbidden

run "printf" with arguments [""] as findings
for each rule in required
  run "printf" with arguments ["%s\n", rule] as needle
  if proposed contains needle
    run "printf" with arguments ["%spass  requires   %s\n", findings, rule] as findings
  otherwise
    run "printf" with arguments ["%sFAIL  requires   %s\n", findings, rule] as findings
for each rule in forbidden
  run "printf" with arguments ["%s\n", rule] as needle
  if proposed contains needle
    run "printf" with arguments ["%sFAIL  forbids    %s\n", findings, rule] as findings
  otherwise
    run "printf" with arguments ["%spass  forbids    %s\n", findings, rule] as findings

then "grep" with arguments ["-F", "--", "FAIL"] and keep status as s5
then count lines
then parse json as fail_json

title: CI results triage
subtitle: API JSON → page, notify, ignore
source:
# Triage a CI API response (a list of workflow runs) into who needs to act.
#   Main-branch failures page the on-call. Failures on other branches go to the author. Cancelled runs are ignored.
define a program named count_of
  accept text as text
  use value text
  then count lines
  then parse json as measured
  take integer at "" from measured as count
  then encode count as json

read "ci-runs.json"
then parse json as response
take json at "/workflow_runs" from response as runs
take integer at "/total_count" from response as total

run "printf" with arguments [""] as page
run "printf" with arguments [""] as notify
run "printf" with arguments [""] as healthy
run "printf" with arguments [""] as ignored
for each item in runs
  take integer at "/id" from item as id
  take text at "/workflow" from item as workflow
  take text at "/branch" from item as branch
  take text at "/conclusion" from item as conclusion
  take integer at "/minutes" from item as minutes
  if conclusion is "success"
    run "printf" with arguments ["%s#%d %s on %s\n", healthy, id, workflow, branch] as healthy
  otherwise if conclusion is "cancelled"
    run "printf" with arguments ["%s#%d %s on %s\n", ignored, id, workflow, branch] as ignored
  otherwise if branch is "main"
    run "printf" with arguments ["%s#%d %s on main: %s after %d min\n", page, id, workflow, conclusion, minutes] as page
  otherwise
    run "printf" with arguments ["%s#%d %s on %s: %s after %d min\n", notify, id, workflow, branch, conclusion, minutes] as notify

run program count_of with text page as page_count
run program count_of with text notify as notify_count
run program count_of with text healthy as healthy_count
run program count_of with text ignored as ignored_count

if page_count is "0"
  run "printf" with arguments ["main is green"] as status

# Plan a backup rotation without deleting anything: keep the newest N, keep the first of each month, delete the rest.
# Dates in the names sort as text, so a reverse sort puts the newest first.
accept keep as integer with default 7

read "backups.json"
then parse json as inventory
take json at "/backups" from inventory as backups

# Pass 1: collect the names.
run "printf" with arguments [""] as names
for each item in backups
  take text at "/name" from item as name
  run "printf" with arguments ["%s%s\n", names, name] as names

use value names
then "sort" with arguments ["-r"]
pipe to "head" with arguments ["-n", keep] as newest

# Pass 2: decide each backup. Sizes are shown, never summed.

title: Duplicate file finder
subtitle: cksum list → duplicate groups
source:
# Find duplicate files from POSIX cksum output (checksum, size, path), exported as JSON.
#   find ~ -type f -exec cksum {} +   (reduced to cksums.json)
# Files with the same checksum and size are duplicates. Nothing is deleted.
define a program named count_of
  accept text as text
  use value text
  then count lines
  then parse json as measured
  take integer at "" from measured as count
  then encode count as json

read "cksums.json"
then parse json as listing
take json at "/files" from listing as files

# Pass 1: one "checksum size" key per file.
run "printf" with arguments [""] as keys
for each file in files
  take text at "/crc" from file as crc
  take integer at "/bytes" from file as bytes
  run "printf" with arguments ["%s%s %d\n", keys, crc, bytes] as keys

# Pass 2: a file is a duplicate when its key appears on more than one line.
run "printf" with arguments [""] as rows
run "printf" with arguments [""] as groups
for each file in files
  take text at "/crc" from file as crc
  take integer at "/bytes" from file as bytes
  take text at "/path" from file as path
  run "printf" with arguments ["%s %d", crc, bytes] as key
  use value keys
  then "grep" with arguments ["-F", "--", key] and keep status as s1
  then count lines
  then parse json as copies_json
  take integer at "" from copies_json as copies
  if copies is not 1
    run "printf" with arguments ["%s%s %d bytes, %d copies: %s\n", rows, crc, bytes, copies, path] as rows
    run "printf" with arguments ["%s%s\n", groups, key] as groups

use value rows
then "sort" as ordered
run program count_of with text rows as duplicate_files

use value groups
then "sort" with arguments ["-u"]
then count lines
then parse json as groups_json
take integer at "" from groups_json as duplicate_groups

run "printf" with arguments ["%s duplicate files in %d groups. Each group shares one checksum and size.\n\n%s\nKeep one file per group and review the rest before deleting.", duplicate_files, duplicate_groups, ordered]
